values: LCD glass resistance, area and capacitance
Vendor DXF: bottom contacts, including COM feeds up the left side. First/last follow connected ITO paths.
Glass only. 30 Ω/□ assumed. See Method for terminal definitions, mesh verification and exclusions.
Glass ITO resistance and area-based capacitance estimates. Zebra, PCB and driver impedance are excluded. Density inputs B7:B8 are assumptions, not measurements.
The factory said “30欧”. This workbook assumes 30 Ω/square. Change B4 after confirming the units; all resistance outputs scale linearly.
All contacts are at the bottom. Ideal voltage clamp on the outer 1.5 mm strip of each 1 × 3 mm contact, representing half usable contact length. The resistance of the rubber itself is excluded.
The entire tested visible island is held at one voltage. All other visible islands retain their finite ITO sheet resistance and float. R equals applied voltage divided by total terminal current.
Nearest and farthest visible islands by shortest connected ITO path from the contact. Eight-neighbor geometric paths use the 0.025 mm mesh. They are not straight-line distances.
First/last by path length need not be the lowest/highest resistance islands on a branched electrode. The main table gives full-sheet R to those two stated islands.

Four-neighbor 2D sheet resistor grid with 30 Ω per square cell adjacency. Solve the Dirichlet voltage problem and integrate contact current. The raw first/last square coefficients are in Electrodes columns L:M.
Nine representative electrodes were rerun at 0.020 mm. Maximum resistance change was 12.35%. These are numerical estimates, not exact or fabricated resistance measurements.
All 64 raster conductors remained connected to their source contact. No disconnected conductor area was discarded at the report mesh.
Analytic polygon shoelace area, subtracting holes, using final DXF SEGMENT HATCH boundaries. Narrow routing and contacts are excluded from visible segment area.
780 physical islands, 631 original game segment groups, 664 occupied COM×SEG cells. Cells includes all 768 addresses, with zero area for 104 unused addresses.
Zero-based logical names: COM0 = B-W001 and SEG0 = T-N001. These are glass-net labels, not the replacement driver’s physical SEG pin numbers.
Moida-routing_to_vendor.dxf. Units: mm. HATCH polygons only; duplicate LWPOLYLINE outlines are not counted.
All 780 artwork IDs were matched to final DXF island bounds and area. Electrode assignments were inferred from final conductive polygons and verified by polygon overlap.
Sum of areas over all COMs = sum over all SEGs = sum over all islands = sum over all electrical cells. Resistance equations and area sums remain visible in the workbook.
Do not add first and last resistance: they are two alternative pad-to-island measurements on the same electrode. COM-side and SEG-side values describe different glass conductors.
C = overlap area × assumed pF/mm². Island and game-group C use visible area. Cell/electrode C use full TOP/BOTTOM overlap, including crossing traces. OFF elements remain capacitive loads.
NXP AN11491, §4.3: https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/application-note/AN11491.pdf uses a realistic example of 10 pF/mm². 30 pF/mm² is a sensitivity assumption, not a measured upper bound.
COM sums and SEG sums describe the same capacitors from opposite terminals. Do not add the COM total to the SEG total. Electrode sums assume other electrodes are held at fixed AC potentials.

For one lumped linear RC: τ = R×C; 90%, 95%, 99% settling = 2.303τ, 2.996τ, 4.605τ. The glass is a distributed, coupled network; endpoint R × total net C is only a screening model, not an extracted settling time.
